findings.title: Guard the missing destination calendar before checking Google Meet
findings.body: When destinationCalendar is null, undefined, or empty, destructuring produces an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar. For a Google Meet location, accessing its integration throws instead of falling back to Cal Video as before. Booking creation therefore fails for event types that still select Google Meet after their destination calendar has been removed. Use optional chaining here.

findings.title: Pass each calendar adapter its own destination
findings.body: Every host's credential receives the entire destinationCalendar array. Only the Google adapter selects a destination by credentialId; Office365, Lark, and BaseCalendarService all use the first element. Consequently, a secondary host's Office365 or Lark credential attempts to create an event in the main host's calendar, typically failing with an inaccessible or invalid calendar ID. CalDAV can filter out every calendar and report success without creating anything. Pass a per-destination event to these adapters or make all adapters select by credentialId.

findings.title: Preserve credential IDs on video references
findings.body: This change sets credentialId to undefined for every non-calendar result, discarding the credential ID returned by video meeting creation. handleCancelBooking only deletes a video meeting when its booking reference has a credentialId. Newly created Zoom and other dedicated video bookings will therefore leave their remote meetings active after cancellation. Preserve result.credentialId for video references.

findings.title: Initialize the destination array before adding collective hosts
findings.body: If neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null. The optional push then silently discards all destination calendars collected from the other collective hosts. Those hosts receive no calendar events even when their calendars are connected. Initialize an empty array and append the collected destinations regardless of whether the organizer has one.

findings.title: Retain destination selection for calendars without a credential ID
findings.body: EventManager explicitly supports destination calendars without a credentialId by invoking the credentials matching their integration. This new lookup cannot match such a destination to the numeric credentialId passed to createEvent, so Google always inserts into primary rather than the configured externalId. Existing destinations using that fallback will start putting bookings in the wrong calendar. Preserve the legacy selection when the destination has no credentialId.

findings.title: Cancel recurring events using each reference's credential
findings.body: In the allRemainingBookings branch, the credential resolved for the current host is discarded. The code instead loops only over the booking owner's credentials and selects the first calendar reference from each recurring booking. With multiple collective hosts, this repeats deletion of the first host's events while never deleting the other hosts' events, despite marking every booking cancelled. Iterate each updated booking's calendar references and resolve the corresponding credentialId for each deletion.

findings.title: Reconstruct collective destinations when confirming pending bookings
findings.body: Confirmation reconstructs destinationCalendar with only the booking's single stored destination or the confirming user's destination. The additional collective destinations assembled in handleNewBooking are not persisted on the booking, and this handler does not reload them. Thus collective bookings requiring confirmation still create calendar events for only one host when approved. Reload the participating hosts' destinations before invoking handleConfirmation; the payment confirmation paths need the same treatment.

findings.title: Restore organization slug assignment when team billing is disabled
findings.body: The condition for storing the organization slug has been inverted. With IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED false, organization creation now stores neither slug nor requestedSlug, even though the supplied slug is checked for collisions and used to configure the domain. Self-hosted or other non-billing deployments therefore create organizations without the slug needed to identify their organization URLs. Preserve the previous non-billing slug assignment.
